questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 1 gram of sodium hydroxide was treated with 25 mL of 0.75 M HCl solution, the mass of sodium hydroxide left unreacted is equal to
questions.explanation: NaOH + HCl -> NaCl + H2O. Moles of NaOH = 1/40 = 0.025 mol = 25 millimoles. Millimoles of HCl = M x V = 0.75 x 25 = 18.75 millimoles. Millimoles of NaOH unreacted = 25 - 18.75 = 6.25 millimoles. Mass = 40 x 6.25 = 250 mg.

questions.explanation: Atoms in 4 g He = NA. Atoms in 2.271098 L He at STP = (2.271098/22.4) x NA = 0.101 NA. Atoms in 4 mol He = 4NA. Atoms in 4u He = 4/4 = 1. Hence highest number of atoms is in 4 mol of helium.

questions.topic: Periodic Trends in Properties of Elements
questions.question_text: Arrange the following elements in increasing order of first ionization enthalpy: Li, Be, B, C, N. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: In a period, ionization enthalpy generally increases left to right, but Be(2s2) is more stable than B(2p1) giving Be a higher IE than B. Correct order of first IE: Li < B < Be < C < N.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Intramolecular hydrogen bonding is present in [four structures]

options.a: meta-nitrophenol - benzene ring with NO2 and OH substituents in a 1,3 (meta) relationship (non-adjacent carbons)
options.c: ortho-nitrophenol - benzene ring with NO2 and OH substituents on adjacent carbons (1,2 relationship)
options.d: para-nitrophenol - benzene ring with NO2 and OH substituents directly across the ring from each other (1,4 relationship)

questions.explanation: Intramolecular hydrogen bonding is observed in ortho-nitrophenol (option c), where the -OH and -NO2 groups on adjacent ring carbons are close enough to form a hydrogen bond within the same molecule (forming a six-membered ring via the H-bond). In meta- and para-nitrophenol the groups are too far apart for intramolecular bonding and instead form intermolecular H-bonds; HF also forms only intermolecular H-bonds.

List II (Conditions): I. No heat exchange, II. Carried out at constant temperature, III. Carried out at constant volume, IV. Carried out at constant pressure
questions.explanation: Isothermal -> constant temperature. Isochoric -> constant volume. Isobaric -> constant pressure. Adiabatic -> no heat exchange.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Spontaneity, Entropy, Gibbs Energy Change and Equilibrium
questions.question_text:
In which of the following processes entropy increases?
A. A liquid evaporates to vapour
B. Temperature of a crystalline solid lowered from 130K to 0 K.
C. 2 NaHCO3(s) -> Na2CO3(s) + CO2(g) + H2O(g)
D. Cl2(g) -> 2 Cl(g)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: (A) Liquid to vapour: randomness increases, entropy increases. (B) Cooling 130K to 0K: entropy decreases. (C) Solid to gas products: entropy increases. (D) Cl2(g) -> 2Cl(g): number of gaseous particles increases, entropy increases. Hence entropy increases in A, C, D.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Law of Chemical Equilibrium, Equilibrium Const. and Its Application
questions.question_text: For the reaction 2A <=> B + C, Kc = 4 x 10^-3. At a given time, the composition of reaction mixture is: [A] = [B] = [C] = 2 x 10^-3 M. Then, which of the following is correct?

options.a: Reaction has a tendency to go in backward direction.
options.b: Reaction has gone to completion in forward direction.
options.d: Reaction has a tendency to go in forward direction.

questions.explanation: Qc = [B][C]/[A]^2 = (2x10^-3 x 2x10^-3)/(2x10^-3)^2 = 1. Since Qc (=1) > Kc (=4x10^-3), the reaction has a tendency to go in the backward direction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Law of Chemical Equilibrium, Equilibrium Const. and Its Application
questions.question_text: In which of the following equilibria, Kp and Kc are NOT equal?
questions.explanation: Kp = Kc(RT)^(delta n_gas). For (a), (b) and (d), delta n_gas = 0 so Kp = Kc. For (c), PCl5 -> PCl3 + Cl2, delta n_gas = 1, so Kp = Kc(RT)^1, meaning Kp is NOT equal to Kc.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Redox Reactions (Oxidation and Reduction), Oxidation Number
questions.question_text: Which reaction is NOT a redox reaction?
questions.explanation: In BaCl2 + Na2SO4 -> BaSO4 + 2NaCl, no element changes oxidation state (it is a double displacement/precipitation reaction), so it is not a redox reaction. The other three all involve oxidation state changes.

questions.explanation: 2,3-dimethylbutane has two tertiary (3 degree) carbons at positions 2 and 3.

List II (Number and types of bonds between two carbon atoms): I. one sigma-bond and two pi-bonds, II. two pi-bonds, III. one sigma-bond, IV. one sigma-bond and one pi-bond
questions.explanation: Ethane (C-C): one sigma-bond. Ethene (C=C): one sigma-bond and one pi-bond. C2: two pi-bonds. Ethyne (C-tripleC): one sigma-bond and two pi-bonds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry-Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.question_text: The most stable carbocation among the following is: [four carbocation structures]

options.a: A primary carbocation: cyclopentane ring with an exocyclic =CH2(+) group (cyclopentylmethyl cation) - the positive charge is on a CH2 carbon attached to only one other carbon.
options.b: A tertiary carbocation: cyclohexane ring where one ring carbon bears both a CH3 substituent and the positive charge (1-methylcyclohexan-1-ylium) - that carbon is attached to three other carbons (two ring bonds plus the methyl).
options.c: A secondary carbocation: CH3-CH(+)-CH(CH3)-CH3 (3-methylbutan-2-ylium) - the positively charged carbon is attached to two other carbons and one hydrogen.
options.d: A secondary carbocation: CH3-CH(+)-CH2-CH(CH3)-CH3 (4-methylpentan-2-ylium) - the positively charged carbon is attached to two other carbons and one hydrogen.

questions.explanation: Stability order of carbocations: tertiary > secondary > primary. Option (b) is a tertiary carbocation (the charged ring carbon carries three carbon substituents: two ring bonds plus the methyl group), making it the most stable of the four.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry-Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.topic: Methods of Purification, Qualitative and Quantitative Analysis of Organic Compounds
questions.question_text: On heating some solid substances change from solid to vapour state without passing through liquid state. The technique used for the purification of such solid substances based on the above principle is known as
questions.explanation: This solid-to-vapour-without-liquid phenomenon and the purification technique based on it is called sublimation, used to separate sublimable compounds from non-sublimable impurities.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The boiling point of three isomeric pentanes follows the order n-pentane > isopentane > neopentane
Statement II: When branching increases, the molecule attains a shape of sphere. This results in smaller surface area for contact, due to which the intermolecular forces between the spherical molecules are weak, thereby lowering the boiling point.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.a: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
options.b: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
options.c: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
options.d: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.

questions.explanation: Boiling point decreases with increasing branching because intermolecular (van der Waals) forces decrease as the molecule becomes more spherical (smaller surface area for contact): n-pentane > isopentane > neopentane. Both statements are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The Henry's law constant (KH) values of three gases (A, B, C) in water are 145, 2 x 10^-5 and 35 kbar, respectively. The solubility of these gases in water follow the order:
questions.explanation: Lower KH means higher solubility. KH: B(2x10^-5) < C(35) < A(145). So solubility order: B > C > A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match List I with List II.
List I (Conversion): A. 1 mol of H2O to O2, B. 1 mol of MnO4- to Mn2+, C. 1.5 mol of Ca from molten CaCl2, D. 1 mol of FeO to Fe2O3
List II (Number of Faraday required): I. 3F, II. 2F, III. 1F, IV. 5F

questions.topic: Temperature Dependence of the Rate of a Reaction & Effect of Catalysts
questions.question_text: Activation energy of any chemical reaction can be calculated if one knows the value of

options.a: orientation of reactant molecules during collision
options.b: rate constant at two different temperatures

questions.explanation: Using the Arrhenius-derived formula log(k2/k1) = (Ea/2.303R)(1/T1 - 1/T2), the activation energy Ea can be calculated from the rate constant at two different temperatures.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Temperature Dependence of the Rate of a Reaction & Effect of Catalysts
questions.question_text: Which plot of ln k vs 1/T is consistent with Arrhenius equation? [four ln k vs 1/T graphs]

options.a: A straight line starting near the origin with a positive slope (ln k increases as 1/T increases).
options.b: A straight line with a positive y-intercept and a negative slope, decreasing from upper-left to lower-right, crossing the 1/T axis.
options.c: A straight line starting below the origin (negative y-intercept) with a positive slope, crossing the 1/T axis and continuing upward.
options.d: A straight line with a positive y-intercept and a positive slope, increasing from upper-left.

questions.explanation: The Arrhenius equation ln k = -(Ea/R)(1/T) + ln A is a straight line with NEGATIVE slope (-Ea/R, since Ea and R are both positive) and a positive y-intercept (ln A). Option (b) - a line with positive y-intercept and negative slope - is the only one matching this.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The boiling point of hydrides of Group 16 elements follow the order H2O > H2Te > H2Se > H2S.
Statement II: On the basis of molecular mass, H2O is expected to have lower boiling point than the other members of the group but due to the presence of extensive H-bonding in H2O, it has higher boiling point.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.a: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
options.b: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
options.c: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
options.d: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

questions.explanation: The boiling point order H2O > H2Te > H2Se > H2S is correct, and it is indeed due to extensive hydrogen bonding in H2O overriding the expected trend based on molecular mass. Both statements are true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Among Group 16 elements, which one does NOT show -2 oxidation state?
questions.explanation: Po does not show a -2 oxidation state because electropositive (metallic) character increases going down the group, and Po behaves more metallically.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The E deg value for the Mn3+/Mn2+ couple is more positive than that of Cr3+/Cr2+ or Fe3+/Fe2+ due to change of
questions.explanation: The much larger third ionisation energy of Mn (where the required change is d5 to d4, moving away from the extra-stable half-filled d5 configuration) is mainly responsible for the more positive E deg value; this also explains why the +3 state of Mn is of little importance.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
'Spin only' magnetic moment is same for which of the following ions?
A. Ti3+   B. Cr2+   C. Mn2+   D. Fe2+   E. Sc3+
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Spin-only magnetic moment = sqrt(n(n+2)) BM. Ti3+(d1): 1.73 BM. Cr2+(d4): 4.90 BM. Mn2+(d5): 5.92 BM. Fe2+(d6): 4.90 BM. Sc3+(d0): 0. B(Cr2+) and D(Fe2+) both equal 4.90 BM.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I (Complex): A. [Co(NH3)5(NO2)]Cl2, B. [Co(NH3)5(SO4)]Br, C. [Co(NH3)6][Cr(CN)6], D. [Co(H2O)6]Cl3
List-II (Type of isomerism): I. Solvate isomerism, II. Linkage isomerism, III. Ionization isomerism, IV. Coordination isomerism
questions.explanation: [Co(NH3)5(NO2)]Cl2 shows linkage isomerism (linkage isomer [Co(NH3)5(ONO)]Cl2). [Co(NH3)5(SO4)]Br shows ionization isomerism (isomer [Co(NH3)5Br]SO4). [Co(NH3)6][Cr(CN)6] shows coordination isomerism (isomer [Cr(NH3)6][Co(CN)6]). [Co(H2O)6]Cl3 shows solvate isomerism (isomer [Co(H2O)5Cl]Cl2.H2O). So A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Both [Co(NH3)6]3+ and [CoF6]3- complexes are octahedral but differ in their magnetic behaviour.
Statement II: [Co(NH3)6]3+ is diamagnetic whereas [CoF6]3- is paramagnetic.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.a: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
options.b: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
options.c: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
options.d: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

questions.explanation: Both complexes are octahedral (coordination number 6). NH3 is a strong-field ligand causing pairing in Co3+ (d6) -> diamagnetic. F- is a weak-field ligand, no pairing -> paramagnetic. Both statements are true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Haloarenes and Chemical Reactions of Haloarenes
questions.question_text: The compound that will undergo SN1 reaction with the fastest rate is [four structures]

options.a: Bromobenzene - an aryl bromide (Br directly attached to the aromatic ring).
options.b: 1-Bromo-1-phenylethane - a benzylic secondary bromide, phenyl-CH(CH3)-Br (Br on a carbon directly attached to the benzene ring).
options.c: Cyclohexylmethyl bromide - a primary bromide, cyclohexane-CH2-Br (Br on a carbon attached to the ring but not benzylic).
options.d: Bromocyclohexane - a secondary, non-benzylic bromide, Br directly on a cyclohexane ring carbon.

questions.explanation: SN1 reactions proceed fastest when the intermediate carbocation is resonance-stabilised. Option (b) ionises to a benzylic carbocation that is resonance-stabilised by the adjacent aromatic ring, making it react fastest via SN1. Option (a) is an aryl halide (does not undergo SN1 at all). Options (c) and (d) give non-resonance-stabilised primary/secondary carbocations.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which one of the following alcohols reacts instantaneously with Lucas reagent? [four alcohol structures]

options.b: (CH3)3C-OH (tert-butanol) - a tertiary alcohol, with three methyl groups attached to the carbinol carbon.

questions.explanation: Tertiary alcohols react with Lucas reagent (conc. HCl + ZnCl2) instantaneously via a fast SN1 mechanism (stable tertiary carbocation). Secondary alcohols react within about 5 minutes; primary alcohols do not react at ordinary temperature. Option (b), tert-butanol, is the tertiary alcohol and reacts instantaneously.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match List I with List II.
List I (Reaction, shown as structures): A. A symmetrical alkene (two cyclohexyl groups joined by a C=C) -> 2 equivalents of cyclohexanone. B. Benzene -> benzophenone (diphenyl ketone, Ph-CO-Ph). C. Cyclohexanol (-OH) -> Cyclohexanone (=O). D. Ethylbenzene (Ph-CH2CH3) -> Potassium benzoate (Ph-COOK).
List II (Reagents/Condition): I. Benzoyl chloride (PhCOCl) / Anhyd. AlCl3, II. CrO3, III. KMnO4/KOH, heat, IV. (i) O3 (ii) Zn-H2O
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: A: ozonolysis [(i) O3 (ii) Zn-H2O] of the symmetrical alkene cleaves the C=C to give 2 equivalents of cyclohexanone -> A-IV. B: Friedel-Crafts acylation of benzene with benzoyl chloride/anhydrous AlCl3 gives benzophenone -> B-I. C: oxidation of the secondary alcohol cyclohexanol to the ketone cyclohexanone uses CrO3 -> C-II. D: side-chain oxidation of ethylbenzene to benzoic acid (isolated as its potassium salt) uses hot alkaline KMnO4 -> D-III. So A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Identify the correct reagents that would bring about the following transformation: cyclohexane-CH2-CH=CH2 (allylcyclohexane) -> cyclohexane-CH2-CH2-CHO (3-cyclohexylpropanal)
questions.explanation: Hydroboration-oxidation [(i) BH3 (ii) H2O2/OH-] adds water anti-Markovnikov, giving the primary alcohol cyclohexane-CH2-CH2-CH2OH. PCC (a mild oxidant) then oxidises this primary alcohol to the aldehyde without over-oxidising to the carboxylic acid, giving the target aldehyde. So option (d).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Physical Properties and Chemical Reactions of Aldehydes and Ketones
questions.question_text: Fehling's solution 'A' is

options.a: alkaline solution of sodium potassium tartrate (Rochelle's salt)

questions.explanation: Fehling's solution 'A' is aqueous copper sulphate; Fehling's solution 'B' is the alkaline sodium potassium tartrate (Rochelle's salt) solution.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Aniline does not undergo Friedel-Crafts alkylation reaction.
Statement II: Aniline cannot be prepared through Gabriel synthesis.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.a: Statement I is correct but Statement II is false.
options.b: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true.
options.c: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
options.d: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

questions.explanation: Aniline does not undergo Friedel-Crafts reactions because it forms a salt with the anhydrous AlCl3 Lewis-acid catalyst, deactivating the nitrogen. Gabriel synthesis only prepares aliphatic primary amines (aryl halides do not undergo the required nucleophilic substitution), so aniline cannot be made this way. Both statements are true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
The reagents with which glucose does not react to give the corresponding tests/products are
A. Tollen's reagent   B. Schiff's reagent
C. HCN   D. NH2OH
E. NaHSO3
Choose the correct options from the given below:
questions.explanation: Despite having an aldehyde group, glucose does NOT give a positive Schiff's test (B) and does NOT form the hydrogensulphite addition product with NaHSO3 (E), due to its predominant cyclic (hemiacetal) structure in solution. It does react with Tollen's reagent, HCN, and NH2OH.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: A compound X contains 32% of A, 20% of B and remaining percentage of C. Then, the empirical formula of X is: (Given atomic masses of A = 64; B = 40; C = 32u)
questions.explanation: C% = 100-32-20 = 48%. Mole ratio: A=32/64=0.5, B=20/40=0.5, C=48/32=1.5. Dividing by smallest (0.5): A:B:C = 1:1:3. Empirical formula is ABC3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Identify the correct answer.

options.a: Dipole moment of NF3 is greater than that of NH3.
options.b: Three canonical forms can be drawn for CO3(2-) ion
options.c: Three resonance structures can be drawn for ozone.

questions.explanation: NH3 has a higher dipole moment (4.9x10^-30 Cm) than NF3 (0.8x10^-30 Cm) due to opposing bond-dipole and lone-pair contributions in NF3, so (a) is false. CO3^2- has three canonical (resonance) forms - (b) is TRUE. Ozone has only two resonance structures, not three, so (c) is false. BF3 is trigonal planar with zero net dipole moment, so (d) is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Ionization of Acids & Bases, pH Scale, Hydrolysis
questions.question_text: Consider the following reaction in a sealed vessel at equilibrium with concentrations of N2 = 3.0 x 10^-3 M, O2 = 4.2 x 10^-3 M and NO = 2.8 x 10^-3 M. 2NO(g) <=> N2(g) + O2(g). If 0.1 mol/L of NO(g) is taken in a closed vessel, what will be degree of dissociation (alpha) of NO(g) at equilibrium?
questions.explanation: Kc = [N2][O2]/[NO]^2 = (3x10^-3 x 4.2x10^-3)/(2.8x10^-3)^2 = 1.6 (approx). With initial NO = 0.1M, at equilibrium NO=(0.1-0.1 alpha), N2=O2=0.1 alpha/2. Solving (0.1 alpha/2)^2 / (0.1-0.1 alpha)^2 = 1.6 gives alpha ~ 0.717.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: For the given reaction: a 1,2-disubstituted alkene, cyclohexyl-CH=CH-cyclohexyl (dicyclohexylethylene, with an H shown on the left alkene carbon), treated with KMnO4/H+ to give major product 'P'. 'P' is: [four structural options]

options.a: cyclohexane-CH(OH)-CH(OH)-cyclohexane - a vicinal diol (product of cold, dilute KMnO4 - syn-dihydroxylation).
options.c: cyclohexane-CHO - an aldehyde (single ring shown with a CHO substituent).

questions.explanation: The starting alkene is disubstituted with one H remaining on each double-bond carbon (Cy-CH=CH-Cy). Hot, acidified (strong) KMnO4 cleaves the C=C bond oxidatively; since each alkene carbon bears one H, oxidative cleavage carries each fragment all the way to a carboxylic acid (not stopping at an aldehyde or diol, which would require a milder oxidant or a fully-substituted alkene). So P = cyclohexanecarboxylic acid, option (d).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Colligative Properties and Determination of Molar Mass
questions.question_text: The plot of osmotic pressure (P) vs concentration (mol L-1) for a solution gives a straight line with slope 25.73 L bar mol-1. The temperature at which the osmotic pressure measurement is done is: (Use R = 0.083 L bar mol-1 K-1)
questions.explanation: pi = CRT, so slope = RT = 25.73. T = 25.73/0.083 = 310 K = 37 degC.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Introduction and Werner's Theory of Coordination Compounds
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: [Co(NH3)6]3+ is a homoleptic complex whereas [Co(NH3)4Cl2]+ is a heteroleptic complex.
Statement II: Complex [Co(NH3)6]3+ has only one kind of ligands but [Co(NH3)4Cl2]+ has more than one kind of ligands.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.a: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
options.b: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
options.c: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
options.d: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

questions.explanation: A homoleptic complex contains only one kind of ligand; a heteroleptic complex contains two or more kinds. [Co(NH3)6]3+ has only NH3 ligands (homoleptic); [Co(NH3)4Cl2]+ has both NH3 and Cl- (heteroleptic). Both statements are true and Statement II correctly explains Statement I.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Haloalkanes and Chemical Reactions of Haloalkanes
questions.question_text: Major products A and B formed in the following reaction sequence, are: 2-methylcyclohexan-1-ol (H3C at C2, OH at C1, adjacent on the ring) --PBr3--> A (major) --alc. KOH, heat--> B (major). [four A/B structure-pair options]

options.a: A = a ring bearing H3C, OH, and Br all together (an inconsistent/distractor structure retaining the original OH alongside a new Br); B = a ring bearing H3C, OH and a ring double bond.
options.b: A = a ring bearing H3C, OH and Br together (same inconsistency as (a)); B = a ring bearing H3C with a ketone (C=O) group.
options.c: A = 1-bromo-2-methylcyclohexane (H3C and Br on adjacent ring carbons, OH fully replaced); B = a methylcyclohexene with the ring double bond positioned to give the more substituted (Zaitsev/major) alkene.
options.d: A = 1-bromo-2-methylcyclohexane (same as option c); B = a methylcyclohexene with the ring double bond at a different (less substituted) position than option c.

questions.explanation: PBr3 converts the secondary alcohol (2-methylcyclohexan-1-ol) to the corresponding bromide A = 1-bromo-2-methylcyclohexane (full substitution of OH by Br, options a and b showing OH retained alongside Br are inconsistent with a simple substitution and are distractors). Alcoholic KOH under heat then performs elimination (dehydrohalogenation) of A; per Zaitsev's rule the major product B is the more substituted (more stable) methylcyclohexene, matching option (c)'s double-bond position rather than option (d)'s.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
The products A and B obtained in the following reactions, respectively, are:
3ROH + PCl3 -> 3RCl + A
ROH + PCl5 -> RCl + HCl + B
questions.explanation: 3ROH + PCl3 -> 3RCl + H3PO3 (A = H3PO3). ROH + PCl5 -> RCl + HCl + POCl3 (B = POCl3). So A = H3PO3, B = POCl3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Identify the major product C formed in the following reaction sequence: CH3-CH2-CH2-I --NaCN--> A --(partial hydrolysis, OH-)--> B --(NaOH, Br2)--> C (major)
questions.explanation: CH3CH2CH2-I + NaCN -> CH3CH2CH2-CN (A, butanenitrile). Partial hydrolysis of nitrile A gives the amide CH3CH2CH2-CONH2 (B, butanamide). Hofmann bromamide degradation (NaOH/Br2) of amide B converts it to a primary amine with one fewer carbon: propylamine (C). So the major product C is propylamine, option (c).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Preparation of Organic and Inorganic Compounds
questions.question_text: During the preparation of Mohr's salt solution (Ferrous ammonium sulphate), which of the following acid is added to prevent hydrolysis of Fe2+ ion?
questions.explanation: Fe2+ ion undergoes hydrolysis, so while preparing the aqueous solution of ferrous sulphate (as part of Mohr's salt preparation), 2-3 mL of dilute sulphuric acid is added to prevent hydrolysis.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are certain cations. Using inorganic qualitative analysis, arrange them in increasing group number from 0 to VI.
A. Al3+   B. Cu2+   C. Ba2+   D. Co2+   E. Mg2+
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Qualitative analysis groups: Cu2+ - Group 2, Al3+ - Group 3, Co2+ - Group 4, Ba2+ - Group 5, Mg2+ - Group 6. Increasing group order: B(Cu2+, gp2), A(Al3+, gp3), D(Co2+, gp4), C(Ba2+, gp5), E(Mg2+, gp6) i.e. B, A, D, C, E.
